summary: 切叶蚁用植物材料栽培真菌，不同工蚁分工维持菌园。几种切叶蚁依赖同一种栽培菌，容易受到寄生霉菌威胁，而蚁体共生细菌能帮助保护菌园。

paragraphs.brief: 只有一个切叶的巢穴可能包含一千个这样的洞穴，深达18英尺的地下大都市，并且支持一个有100多万蚂蚁的社会。
sentences: Leaf-cutting ants and their fungus ‘farm’ are a marvel of nature and perhaps the best-known example of symbiosis — the mutual dependence of two species.
切叶蚁及其真菌 " 农场 " 是大自然的奇迹，或许也是最著名的共生的例子，即两个物种的相互依存关系。
Ants cultivate a mushroom-like fungus in ‘farms’.
蚂蚁在「农场」培育蘑菇般的真菌。
Both the ants and their so-called ‘agriculture’ have been extensively studied over the years, but recent research has uncovered intriguing new findings.
蚂蚁和他们所谓的“农业”多年来都受到广泛研究，但最近的研究发现了令人感兴趣的新发现。
Ants invented agriculture 50 million years before people did, and the leaf-cutters, members of the large attine ant family, practise the most sophisticated example of it.
蚂蚁比人类早 5,000 万年就发明了农业。切叶蚁属于庞大的菌圃蚁类群，实行的是其中最为精巧的一种农作方式。
They grow their fungus in underground chambers that can reach the size of a football.
他们生长的真菌可以在地下室内达到足球的大小。
A single leaf-cutter nest may contain a thousand such chambers, embedded in an underground metropolis up to 18 feet deep, and support a society of more than a million ants.
只有一个切叶的巢穴可能包含一千个这样的洞穴，深达18英尺的地下大都市，并且支持一个有100多万蚂蚁的社会。

paragraphs.brief: 蚂蚁的成就是惊人的，因为它允许它们利用蘑菇的消化能力，收获树叶上充满有毒化学品的热带森林。
sentences: These ant communities are the dominant plant-eaters of the Neotropics, the region comprising South and Central America, Mexico and the Caribbean.
这些蚂蚁社区是新热带地区的主要植物食用者，该地区包括南美洲和中美洲、墨西哥和加勒比地区。
Biologists believe 15 percent of the leaf production of tropical forests disappears down the nests of leaf-cutter ants.
生物学家认为热带森林的叶子 15%的产量消失在切叶蚁的巢穴里
In the nest, the leaves are shredded and added to the fungus, which digests the leaves and is in turn eaten by the ants.
在巢中，叶片被切碎并添加到真菌中，消化叶子并反过来被蚂蚁吃掉。

The attine ants’ achievement is remarkable because it allows them to consume, courtesy of their mushroom’s digestive powers, the harvest of tropical forests whose leaves are laden with poisonous chemicals.
蚂蚁的成就是惊人的，因为它允许它们利用蘑菇的消化能力，收获树叶上充满有毒化学品的热带森林。

paragraphs.brief: 已知的阿提纳蚂蚁部落有200多个物种，分为12个组，即基因组。
sentences: There are more than 200 known species of the attine ant tribe, divided into 12 groups, or genera.
已知的阿提纳蚂蚁部落有200多个物种，分为12个组，即基因组。

The leaf-cutters use fresh vegetation; the other groups, known as the lower attines because their nests are smaller and their techniques more primitive, feed their gardens with similar leaves that have fallen on the ground and insects that lie on the forest floor.
切叶者使用新鲜植被；其他群体，即低端阁楼，因为它们的巢穴较小，技术更原始，以落地的类似叶子和森林地上的昆虫喂养花园。
Lower attine ants are all a similar size.
低量的蚂蚁大小都差不多
However, leaf-cutter worker ants come in made-to-fit sizes — large ants to saw off leaves, medium ones to shred them, and miniature workers to seed them with fungus and clean off alien growths.
然而，切叶工人蚂蚁的尺寸是按适量计算的——大蚂蚁锯掉叶子，中型蚂蚁切碎叶子，微型工人用真菌播种，清洗外星生长。

paragraphs.brief: 1994年，美国农业部的生物学家分析了蚂蚁真菌的DNA。
sentences: In 1994, biologists from the United States Department of Agriculture analysed the DNA of ant fungi.
1994年，美国农业部的生物学家分析了蚂蚁真菌的DNA。
They found that the leaf-cutters’ fungus was descended from a single pure strain, propagated for at least 23 million years.
他们发现切叶机的真菌是从一个纯菌株中降下来的传播至少2300万年
However, the fungi grown by lower attine ants fell into four different groups, as if the ants had domesticated wild fungi at least four times in evolutionary history.
然而，低量蚂蚁生长的真菌分为四个不同组别，好像蚂蚁在进化史上至少把野生真菌养成四次。
What could be driving these two patterns of fungus gardening — the pure clone cultivation of the leaf-cutters and the multiple varieties of the lower attines?
是什么驱动了这两种真菌园艺模式——纯克隆的切叶机种植和低端阁楼的多种品种？

paragraphs.brief: 然而，Currie在经过三年的刺青蚂蚁园后发现了几个外来生物，特别是一个叫作“Escovopsis”的寄生虫模型家族。
sentences: The answer has been suggested by Cameron Currie of the University of Toronto.
多伦多大学的Cameron Currie提出了答案。
The pure strain of fungus grown by the leaf-cutters, it seemed to him, resembled the single crops grown by humans to the exclusion of all others, such as potato growing.
他似乎认为，切叶者生长的纯真菌菌株与人类生长的单一作物相似，而排斥所有其他作物，如土豆种植。

These ‘monocultures’, which lack the genetic diversity to respond to changing environmental threats, are particularly vulnerable to parasites — organisms that live and feed on their host, often causing harm.
这些“海洋养殖”缺乏应对不断变化的环境威胁的遗传多样性，特别容易受到寄生虫的伤害，寄生虫是寄生虫生存和食用其宿主的有机体，往往造成伤害。
Currie felt there had to be a parasite in the ant-fungus system.
Currie觉得蚂蚁体内一定有寄生虫
But a century of ant research had provided no evidence for his idea.
但是一个世纪的蚂蚁研究没有提供证据证明他的想法。
Textbooks describe how leaf-cutter ants scrupulously weed their gardens of all foreign organisms.
教科书描述了切叶蚂蚁如何小心地除去所有外来生物的花园。
“People kept telling me the ants keep their gardens free of parasites,” said Currie.
Currie说的：“人们一直告诉我蚂蚁没有寄生虫的花园。”
Nevertheless, after three years of sifting through attine ant gardens, Currie discovered several alien organisms, particularly a family of parasitic moulds called ‘Escovopsis’.
然而，Currie在经过三年的刺青蚂蚁园后发现了几个外来生物，特别是一个叫作“Escovopsis”的寄生虫模型家族。

paragraphs.brief: 显然，蚂蚁通常设法控制住寄生虫和其他寄生虫。
sentences: Escovopsis is a deadly disease that can devastate a fungus garden in a couple of days.
复古是一种致命的疾病几天后就能摧毁一个真菌花园
It blooms like a white cloud which envelops the whole garden.
它开得像白色的云笼罩着整个花园
Other ants won’t go near it, and the ants associated with the garden just starve to death.
其他的蚂蚁不会靠近它和花园有关的蚂蚁只是饿死而已
Evidently, the ants usually manage to keep Escovopsis and other parasites under control.
显然，蚂蚁通常设法控制住寄生虫和其他寄生虫。
Nevertheless, with any lapse in control Escovopsis will quickly burst forth.
然而，随着控制失效，埃斯科沃普西将很快爆发。
Although new leaf-cutter gardens start off free of Escovopsis, within two years some 60 percent become infected.
虽然新的叶片园区开始免费的Escovopsis，但两年内，大约60%的人感染了。

paragraphs.brief: 发现Escovopsis的作用，使人们对阁楼蚂蚁的演变有了新的了解。
sentences: The discovery of Escovopsis’s role brings a new level of understanding to the evolution of the attine ants.
发现Escovopsis的作用，使人们对阁楼蚂蚁的演变有了新的了解。
In the last decade, evolutionary biologists have been increasingly aware of the role of parasites as driving forces in evolution.
在过去十年中，进化生物学家越来越认识到寄生虫作为进化动力的作用。
With Currie’s work, there is now a possible reason for the different varieties of fungus in the lower attine mushroom gardens — to stay one step ahead of the relentless Escovopsis.
现在，随着Currie的工作，在低端的庭院蘑菇园中，可能有各种真菌，比无情的迷魂药园早一步。
Interestingly, the leaf-cutters had, in general, fewer alien moulds in their gardens than the lower attines, yet more Escovopsis infections.
有趣的是，一般而言，剪叶师的花园中外形比低端的阁楼少，但感染者却更多。
Clearly, the price they pay for cultivating a pure variety of fungus is a higher risk from Escovopsis.
显然，他们为培育纯粹种类的真菌付出的代价是Escovopsis的更大风险。

paragraphs.brief: 令人惊讶的是，叶片蚂蚁正在超越人类的力量而取得成就：它们年复一年地种植单一文化作物，没有发生灾难，而且它们显然非常明智地使用抗生素，因此，与人们不同，它们不会在产生疾病的目标生物体中产生抗生素抗药性。
sentences: So how do attine ants keep this parasite under control?
宫内蚂蚁如何控制这种寄生虫？
People have known for a hundred years that ants have a whitish growth on their body surface.
人们已经知道一百年了蚂蚁在身体表面有微小的生长

It was thought to be wax but, after examining it under a microscope, Currie discovered a specialised patch on the ants’ bodies that harbours a particular kind of bacterium, one well known to the pharmaceutical industry and the source of half the antibiotics used in medicine.
它被认为是蜡，但在用显微镜检查之后，Currie在蚂蚁身上发现了一个专门贴有某种细菌的斑点，这是制药业所熟知的，也是药物中一半抗生素的来源。
This bacterium is a potent poisoner of Escovopsis, inhibiting its growth and suppressing spore formation.
这种细菌是埃斯科沃普西的强效毒药，抑制其生长，抑制了猪卵的形成。

Astoundingly, the leaf-cutter ants are accomplishing feats beyond the power of humans: they are growing a monocultural crop year after year without disaster, and they are using an antibiotic apparently so wisely that, unlike people, they are not provoking antibiotic resistance in the target disease-producing organism.
令人惊讶的是，叶片蚂蚁正在超越人类的力量而取得成就：它们年复一年地种植单一文化作物，没有发生灾难，而且它们显然非常明智地使用抗生素，因此，与人们不同，它们不会在产生疾病的目标生物体中产生抗生素抗药性。

items.en: two things at which leaf-cutter ants have succeeded but humans have failed.
items.zh: 两件事叶片切蚂蚁成功但人类失败了
items.why: H段并列两项成就：切叶蚁长期单一种植而未遭灾难，同时其防治手段似乎未引起寄生菌耐药。

items.en: a comparison between the nests of leaf-cutter ants and lower attine ants.
items.zh: 与叶片蚂蚁的巢穴和小蚂蚁之间的对比。
items.why: 题干: a comparison between the nests of /eaf-cutter ants and lower attine ants。C段直接比较: 叶切蚁用“新鲜植被" 且巢穴更大。下位阿庭蚁用“落在地上的小叶和昆虫”,巢更小。这是唯一同时比较“食材 /做法/巢大小”的段落。排除: A段虽有“巨大地下室”“上千房间”,但未与下位阿庭蚁对照。因此真正的“比较"在C段。

items.en: an assessment of the impact leaf-cutter ants have on their environment.
items.zh: 对切叶蚁对环境的影响进行评估。
items.why: 题干: an assessment of the impact…on their environment。B段量化了影 I: 主导性植食者，且吞入森林15% 叶产量。并解释通过真菌消化使有毒叶片也能被利用-一这是对生态影响的评价。排除: 其它段落多为分类、进化或防治机制，并无环境“影响评估”。

items.en: the effect Escovopsis has on ant communities.
items.why: 文中说这种寄生霉菌几天内就能毁掉菌园，会危及蚁群赖以为生的食物来源。

items.en: the advantage for lower attine ants of growing a range of fungi.
items.zh: 长出一系列真菌有利于低量蚂蚁生长
items.why: 题干 : the advantage for Jower attine ants of growing a range of fungi。 G 段给出优势 : 多样化真菌有助于领先寄生霉一步，降低风险。这正是“种类多”的好处。排除 : D/E 段谈“单一纯株 / 单一作物”的叶切蚁，不符合“lower attines 的优势”。

items.en: the discovery of the age of the attine-ant fungi.
items.zh: 发现阿提恩真菌的年龄
items.why: 题干: the discovery of the age of the attine-ant fungi。D段给出至少2300 万年的时间尺度，属于“真菌培养谱系的年代/年龄发现。排除: 其余段落无年代信息。

items.en: the use of dead vegetation to cultivate their fungus
items.zh: 利用死亡植被培育真菌

items.en: very small ants that keep the fungus free of foreign organisms
items.zh: 非常小的蚂蚁使真菌远离外国生物

items.en: the ability to safely eat harmful plants
items.zh: 安全地食用有害植物的能力
items.answer: C · Both leaf-cutting ants and lower attine ants

items.en: the cultivation of a single fungus
a nest with a very large number of rooms for growing fungus
items.zh: 巢穴里有很多生长真菌的房间

items.en: What does the writer say about Cameron Currie’s research?
items.zh: 卡梅伦·科里的研究如何？
correct: Earlier studies did not support his theory.
先前的研究并不支持他的理论。

items.en: Using a microscope, Currie was the first to discover that the body of attine ants
items.zh: 使用显微镜，Currie是第一个发现原子蚁体
correct: has a substance useful to humans.
具有对人类有用的物质。

points: 文中说这种寄生霉菌几天内就能毁掉菌园，会危及蚁群赖以为生的食物来源。
题干问“种植单一真菌”。定位句写到“他们发现切叶机的真菌是从一个纯菌株中降下来的传播至少2300万年”。
clauses: Ants invented agriculture …, and the leaf-cutters, members of the large attine ant family, practise the most sophisticated example of it.
连接词 before 引出“50 million years before people did”，说明主句的时间关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 before 把这一层关系补进去。
They grow their fungus in underground chambers ….
“that can reach the size of a football”修饰前面的 fungus。先认出先行词，再读从句补充的特征。
读到 that 时，回看 fungus，再把修饰信息接回主句。
lead: Nicholas Wade examines leaf-cutter ants and their amazing agriculture
尼古拉斯・韦德检查切叶蚁及其惊人的农业
